penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Salesforce platform quirks are highly context-specific; support questions from consulting customers will require judgment calls about org configuration, API version, and data model — not fully automatable.

rationale: The buyer is a named professional (Salesforce LWC developer or consultant at a firm) with real budget authority and an hourly-rate incentive to resolve blockers fast — that's a genuine strength. However, the market is narrow (LWC compound-field issues are a specific platform bug, not a broad workflow gap), the signal is a single forum post (signal_strength 2), and there is no tested responsiveness signal at all. After the high-touch-support penalty the total falls to 5.0, just below the validate threshold of 5.5. The opportunity is better framed as a content/SEO play (a free detailed workaround article that drives consulting leads) than a paid micro-service.
solution_plan: This idea sits just below the validate threshold and should be dropped in its current form. A paid LWC utility library for compound field normalization is technically buildable (Claude can help draft Apex/JS code and documentation), but the market is too narrow and the support burden too high for an autonomous product: every Salesforce org has a unique data model, so customers would need custom help rather than a generic tool. If Youval wanted to probe this space, the right low-cost test is publishing a detailed free article (with a 'hire me for Salesforce consulting' CTA) rather than building a product — but that is a content strategy, not a factory-built autonomous service. Recommend drop and re-evaluate only if multiple corroborating signals appear across different Salesforce pain points pointing to a broader workflow automation gap.
notes: Total 5.0 is below min_total_to_validate (5.5). Market is too narrow and single-signal. high_touch_support penalty applied.
